TotalReads.note: STAR's "Number of input reads" in <sample>.Log.final.out: reads entering alignment, i.e. post-trim. Not MultiQC's star-total_reads, which is the same number in millions. No samtools fallback: raw_total_sequences counts BAM records (both mates), not reads.

NumAligned.note: STAR's "Uniquely mapped reads number" in <sample>.Log.final.out. Not MultiQC's star-uniquely_mapped, which is in millions.

UnalignedReads.note: sum of STAR's three "unmapped:" lines in <sample>.Log.final.out (too many mismatches + too short + other). NOT total-unique-multi: that also counts "mapped to too many loci", which STAR files under MULTI-MAPPING READS because those reads did align, just to more places than the threshold allows.

5_3UTR.note: Qualimap 5'-3' bias; the alternate is MultiQC <=1.22's name for the same column

rRNAPercent.note: from the featureCounts biotype table; sortmerna only runs under remove_ribo_rna

DuplicationPercent.note: MultiQC writes Picard's fraction as a percentage

MultimappedPercent.note: STAR's % of reads mapped to multiple loci, from Log.final.out's counts

Strandedness.note: forward, reverse or unstranded by nf-core's rule on RSeQC infer_experiment; blank when undetermined

DupRadarIntercept.note: dupRadar's exp(intercept): fitted odds of a duplicate at 1 read per kilobase

MismatchPercent.note: MultiQC writes samtools' error rate as a percentage

deliberately_unmapped.why: MultiQC prints it in millions. TotalReads reads the exact count from the STAR log ($derived.total_reads).
MultiQC prints it in millions. NumAligned reads the exact count from the STAR log ($derived.uniquely_mapped_reads).
In millions, and it counts BAM records (both mates of a pair), not reads, so it is no stand-in for TotalReads.
Strandedness is filled from $derived.strandedness (RSeQC infer_experiment, nf-core's rule), so this key adds nothing.
MultiQC prints it in millions. MultimappedPercent is computed from the STAR log's exact counts ($derived.multimapped_pct).
Meaningful only for multi-run samples; nf-core concatenates before QC, so per-lane percentages are not recoverable.
No nf-core/rnaseq equivalent.
A sequencer capacity figure, not a pipeline output.

Qualimap's count of aligned reads (read pairs, for paired-end data), in millions. Alignment is already recorded from the STAR log: TotalReads, NumAligned (exact uniquely mapped count) and MappedPercent.

Qualimap's count of reads in exons, in millions. The region shares are already recorded as CDSPercent, UTRPercent and the exon ratios, from RSeQC read_distribution; a second tool's raw count adds nothing.
Qualimap's count of reads in introns, in millions. IntronPercent and ExonIntronRatio already record this share, from RSeQC read_distribution.
Qualimap's count of reads in intergenic regions, in millions. IntergenicPercent and ExonIntergenicRatio already record this share, from RSeQC read_distribution.

Qualimap's count, in millions, of intronic or intergenic reads that also overlap an exon. A boundary case of the region split already recorded from RSeQC read_distribution; D.SEQ has no attribute for it and does not need one.

STAR's uniquely mapped plus multimapped reads, in millions (MultiQC adds the two). NumAligned holds the exact uniquely mapped count from the STAR log; the multimapped share belongs in its own percentage, not in this sum.
Salmon's measure of how strand-specific its mappings were. Strand specificity is already recorded as SenseAntisenseRatio, from RSeQC infer_experiment.
STAR's uniquely mapped plus multimapped percent (MultiQC adds the two), so it equals MappedPercent + MultimappedPercent, both already recorded.
Salmon's pseudo-mapped fragment count, in millions. Alignment is already recorded from the STAR log: TotalReads, NumAligned and MappedPercent.
The share of Salmon's mappings consistent with the library type it used: a check on that call, not a property of the sample. Strandedness records the library type itself.
Read through $derived.strandedness when RSeQC infer_experiment did not run, so Strandedness records it as forward, reverse or unstranded; the raw code is not an attribute of its own.
In millions, and it counts BAM records (both mates, plus secondary and supplementary alignments), not reads, so it is no stand-in for TotalReads.
Mapped BAM records in millions, counting each mate and every secondary alignment. NumAligned holds the exact uniquely mapped read count from the STAR log.
Mapped BAM records as a share of all records, not of reads; it sits near 100 on STAR's BAMs, and MappedPercent already holds STAR's own mapped share.
In millions, and it counts mapped BAM records (each mate of a pair), not reads. NumAligned holds the exact uniquely mapped count from the STAR log.
Secondary and supplementary BAM records, in millions: extra records for multimapped reads, which MultimappedPercent already records from the STAR log.
Sits near 100 on STAR's paired-end BAMs and is absent for single-end data, so it tells samples apart by nothing.
RSeQC bam_stat's proper pairs among uniquely mapped reads, divided by every BAM record, so its parts count different things. The properly-paired share is not recorded from samtools either.
STAR gives MAPQ 0 to reads mapped to more than four loci, so this is a slice of the multimapping that MultimappedPercent already records.
Measured on spliced alignments, so introns inflate it far past the real fragment length; it is not a library property worth recording.
